w: Gottfried Semper's 1841 opera house for the Saxon State Opera burned down in 1869; Semper rebuilt it, finishing in 1878. Wagner and Richard Strauss both premiered major works on its stage, and it's still home to the Saxon State Orchestra and the Semperoper Ballett -- three institutions, one theatre, twice built.
s: Wagner premieres in a rebuilt shell
_facts: Built by Gottfried Semper, 1841
Destroyed by fire 1869, rebuilt by Semper, completed 1878
Home to Saxon State Opera, Staatskapelle Dresden, Semperoper Ballett
Premiered major works by Wagner and Richard Strauss

w: Some 750 paintings from the 15th to 18th centuries hang in the Zwinger's Semper Gallery wing -- Italian Renaissance masters alongside Dutch, Flemish, German, French and Spanish painters of the period. It's the Old Masters half of the Dresden State Art Collections, one of the world's oldest museum institutions.
_facts: About 750 paintings, 15th-18th centuries
Located in the Semper Gallery wing of the Zwinger
Part of the Dresden State Art Collections
Includes Italian Renaissance, Dutch and Flemish works

w: A sandstone Renaissance Revival hall on Bruhl's Terrace, named for King Albert of Saxony, houses the New Masters Gallery and the Sculpture Collection of the Dresden State Art Collections -- roughly two hundred years of painting and sculpture, from Romanticism up to the present day, under one royal name.
s: two centuries of German art on Bruhl's Terrace
_facts: Renaissance Revival building on Bruhl's Terrace
Named after King Albert of Saxony
Hosts New Masters Gallery and Sculpture Collection
Covers art from Romanticism to the present, about 200 years

w: Built in 1907-09 as a cigarette factory, its Moorish Revival dome and six hundred windows were pure marketing -- advertising the Ottoman tobacco it processed by dressing the building as a mosque. Locals still call it the Tabakmoschee. It came through the 1945 firebombing almost untouched, dome and all.
s: the tobacco mosque that isn't a mosque
_facts: Built 1907-09 as the Yenidze cigarette factory
Moorish Revival design, 600 windows, 20m dome
Nicknamed the 'tobacco mosque' (Tabakmoschee)
Survived the 1945 bombing of Dresden relatively unharmed

w: The main church of Saxony's Evangelical-Lutheran bishop and the largest church in the entire Free State, its plain tower has watched over the Altmarkt for generations. It's home to the Dresdner Kreuzchor, the boys' choir that has sung its services since long before the war -- Lutheran Dresden's most important pulpit.
s: Saxony's biggest church, sung by boys for centuries
_facts: Main church of the Evangelical-Lutheran Church of Saxony
Largest church building in the Free State of Saxony
Home of the Dresdner Kreuzchor boys' choir

w: Wolfgang Hansch's modernist hall opened in 1969 as East Germany's largest multi-purpose venue -- a stark, unadorned International Style block, sister building to Berlin's since-demolished Palast der Republik. A years-long rebuild gave it a new concert hall in 2017, inside the historic Altmarkt.
s: East Germany's palace of culture, still standing
_facts: Designed by Wolfgang Hansch, opened 1969
Largest multi-purpose hall in Dresden at the time
Sister building to Berlin's demolished Palast der Republik
Reconstructed 2012-2017 with a new concert hall

w: Consecrated in 1720, this was the first Catholic burial ground allowed in Dresden after the Reformation -- and it shows in the density of Baroque, Rococo and Neoclassical monuments packed inside. One of the region's most historically important cemeteries, it's a quiet catalogue of three centuries of Dresden's dead.
s: baroque tombstones on the Elbe's left bank
_facts: Consecrated 1720
First Catholic cemetery in Dresden after the Reformation
Vast number of Baroque, Rococo and Neoclassical tombs
Located in the Friedrichstadt district

w: The Sophienkirche was once Dresden's oldest church -- until the 1945 bombing erased it. This memorial reconstructs its Busmannkapelle chapel, a project twelve years in the building before it opened in 2020 as the DenkRaum Sophienkirche: a small commemorative space standing in for a whole lost church.
s: twelve years to rebuild a chapel that vanished
_facts: Sophienkirche was Dresden's oldest church, destroyed in 1945 bombing
Reconstruction of the Busmannkapelle chapel began 2009 after 1995 planning
Opened as DenkRaum Sophienkirche in 2020

w: Built as the Catholic court church of Saxony's royal family, it became the cathedral of the Diocese of Dresden-Meissen in 1964. Inside lie members of the House of Wettin, including Saxon monarchs who also wore the crown of Poland -- one church, two royal lines, resting together by the Elbe.
s: a royal burial vault for two crowns
_facts: Built as the Catholic court church of Saxony
Became cathedral of the Diocese of Dresden-Meissen in 1964
Burial site of the House of Wettin, including Polish monarchs

w: Residence of Saxony's electors and kings for almost 400 years, its Baroque-to-Neo-Renaissance walls now hold a museum complex: the Green Vault treasuries, the Numismatic Cabinet, a print collection, and the armory's Turkish Chamber -- one of the oldest buildings in Dresden, still full of what its rulers collected.
s: four centuries of electors, kings and treasure
_facts: Residence of Saxon electors 1547-1806 and kings 1806-1918
Also seat of Kings of Poland 1697-1763
Now houses the Green Vault, Numismatic Cabinet, print collection, armory

w: A raised architectural promenade high above the Elbe's bank, nicknamed the Balcony of Europe, stretching north of the rebuilt Neumarkt Square in the historic centre. It has framed the same river view for the well-dressed and the sightseeing alike since Dresden was still a royal capital.
s: the Balcony of Europe over the Elbe
_facts: Historic architectural ensemble above the Elbe
Nicknamed 'The Balcony of Europe'
Located north of Neumarkt Square

w: Painted in the 1870s to mark 800 years of Wettin rule, then transferred between 1904 and 1907 onto roughly 23,000 Meissen porcelain tiles so it would survive the weather. At 102 metres, it's the largest porcelain artwork on Earth: 35 rulers on horseback, parading along Dresden Castle's stable-yard wall.
s: 35 rulers, painted then baked into porcelain
_facts: Originally painted 1871-76, marking 800 years of Wettin rule
Transferred to about 23,000 Meissen porcelain tiles 1904-1907
102 metres long, largest porcelain artwork in the world
Depicts 35 rulers of the House of Wettin, 1127-1904

w: A stone bridge has crossed the Elbe here since 1220. Augustus the Strong replaced it with a twelve-arch sandstone span in the 1730s; the current nine-arch version, built 1907-1910, widened the river opening for boat traffic. Trams still rattle across what is essentially Dresden's oldest address.
s: the fourth bridge on an 800-year-old crossing
_facts: First stone bridge on the site built 1220
12-arch bridge built under Augustus the Strong, 1727-1731
Current 9-arch sandstone bridge built 1907-1910
Three Dresden tram lines cross it

w: Completed in 1893 without a single supporting pier in the Elbe -- a marvel for its length at the time -- this cantilever bridge links Loschwitz and Blasewitz, once among Europe's priciest addresses. Dresdeners call it the Blue Wonder, a nod to its paint job and a wink at a German idiom for an unpleasant surprise.
s: the Blue Wonder that needed no river piers
_facts: Completed 1893, cantilever truss bridge, no river piers
Links Blasewitz and Loschwitz districts
Nicknamed 'Blaues Wunder' (Blue Wonder)
Named König-Albert-Brücke after Saxony's King Albert

w: Founded as a one-day market in 1434, it marked its 590th anniversary in 2024 -- among the very first true Christmas markets anywhere. Some 240 stands now fill the Altmarkt each Advent, pulling in about 3 million visitors before the season closes on Christmas Eve.
s: one of the world's oldest Christmas markets
_facts: Founded 1434 as a one-day market
590th anniversary celebrated in 2024
240 stands, about 3 million visitors annually
Runs through Advent until Christmas Eve

w: Formed in 1996 from the merger of Saxony's state library and Dresden University's library, the SLUB holds nearly nine million items -- among them the Codex Dresdensis, long considered the oldest surviving book written in the Americas. Its Deutsche Fotothek wing alone keeps some four million photographs.
s: a Maya codex sleeps in a modern reading room
_facts: Formed 1996 from merger of Saxon State Library and University Library
Nearly 9 million items in its collection
Holds the Codex Dresdensis, oldest surviving book from the Americas
Deutsche Fotothek wing holds about 4 million photographs

n: St. Simeon of the Wonderful Mountain Church
w: Built 1872-74 for Dresden's Russian Orthodox community and dedicated to Simeon Stylites the Younger, this church stood almost untouched through the February 1945 firebombing that gutted the historic centre -- the only building for a wide area to come through relatively intact.
s: the church the 1945 bombs somehow missed
_facts: Built 1872-1874 by Harald Julius von Bosse and Karl Weissbach
Russian Orthodox church, dedicated to Simeon Stylites the Younger
Survived the February 1945 bombing of Dresden largely intact
